newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - July German M3 data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - July German M3 data.

text.p: Following are comments from analysts to July German M3 money supply data, which showed growth at a 5.7 percent annualised rate compared with the 1996 fourth quarter.
"The most important thing is that the press statement from the Bundesbank is a positive response. If they wanted to do some tightening on rates, they would have set up the domestic justification.
"It was reassuring in that sense. It was what they said about M3 that was important, it was positive."
GERHARD GREBE, CHIEF ECONOMIST, BANK JULIUS BAER,FRANKFURT:

"I thought the figures were very good. I was thinking in the same direction myself and expected around 5.9 percent. The strong growth in monetary capital formation was to be expected because of the growth in the markets over July."
"This is very nice for the Bundesbank as it means they can hold off on an interest rate moves for the time being. They can have a nice relaxed Bundesbank meeting on Thursday.
"They are well within the corridor and can sit back."
MICHAEL HOCHGUERTEL, ECONOMIST, BHF BANK, FRANKFURT:
"It is a very good number. I do not expect anything at the moment at the council meeting. Nevertheless, we also know that a decision for a variable rate repo tender is definitely around the corner.

"I think we will see something like that in the near future, towards the end of the year. It will depend on how markets are going. I think dollar-mark is going up again and then the Bundesbnak will introduce a variable-rate tender over the course of the year. But we do not know how much impact that will have because I do not see massive increases in interest rates.
